rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections – just cause required for termination of tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without an enumerated at-fault cause (e.g., nonpayment, material breach, nuisance, criminal activity) or no-fault cause (owner/relative move-in, withdrawal from market, government order, demolition or substantial remodel). The protection applies from the start of the tenancy, and owner move-in for post-6/24/2023 leases requires tenant consent or an express lease clause.
rules.key_value: Just cause required from start of tenancy (>30 days)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including mobilehome-park units, for tenancies longer than 30 days. Excludes fixed-term leases of 3 months or less.
rules.exemptions: Hotels/transient occupancy; short-term rentals; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 still covered); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious, care and transitional housing facilities; school dormitories; units where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with a resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to 2 bedrooms/ADUs/JADUs; owner-occupied two-unit structures; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (not mobilehomes); separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC, if the required exemption notice is given.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for separately alienable units requires a non-corporate/non-REIT owner and a written exemption notice to the tenant (in the lease for tenancies commenced or renewed on/after 2024-01-01). Owner-occupancy and shared-facility exemptions also apply. Excludes affordable/subsidized deed-restricted housing (except Section 8).

rules.penalty: Tenant civil action for injunctive/equitable relief and damages including punitive damages; wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times actual economic damages; discretionary attorney's fees; affirmative defense in an eviction; noncompliant termination notices are void; City civil and criminal enforcement.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.0704 (O-21647 N.S., amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.conflict_note: Amended by O-21769 N.S., effective 2024-03-28. The ordinance is stated to be consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 and adds protections beyond it.

rules.title: San Diego relocation assistance for no-fault terminations
rules.requirement: For any no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must pay relocation assistance of two months' actual rent, or three months' rent if the tenant is a senior (62+) or disabled. The tenant's income and length of tenancy do not matter. The landlord may pay it directly within 15 days of the notice or waive an equivalent amount of rent.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent; 3 months' rent for seniors (62+) or disabled tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in San Diego residential rental property covered by Division 7 that are terminated for no-fault just cause.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as SDMC § 98.0703, including housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years. A tenant found at fault for conditions triggering a government vacate order is not entitled to relocation assistance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to no-fault terminations. Exemption for separately alienable non-corporate-owned units requires a written exemption notice. Owner-occupancy exemptions apply.

rules.penalty: Landlord liable for not less than three times the required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages; the termination notice is void if § 98.0706 is not strictly complied with.
rules.quoted_span: (i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.conflict_note: Relocation assistance is credited against any other federal, state or local relocation assistance.

rules.title: San Diego termination notice requirements and right of first offer after no-fault eviction
rules.requirement: Before an at-fault termination for a curable violation, the landlord must give a cure notice. A no-fault termination notice must state the basis, the relocation assistance and the tenant's re-rental rights. If the unit is re-offered for rent within five years after an owner move-in, government-order or demolition/remodel eviction, the landlord must first offer it to the displaced tenant, provided the tenant requested this in writing within 30 days of the notice. Landlords must also notify the San Diego Housing Commission of terminations within three business days once its portal is established.
rules.key_value: 5-year right of first offer; Commission notice within 3 business days
rules.coverage_conditions: Covered San Diego residential tenancies being terminated for at-fault or no-fault just cause.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Right of first offer requires the tenant's timely written request and an address. The Commission notice requirement applies only 30 days after the Commission establishes a submission portal.

rules.penalty: Any notice of termination is void for failure to strictly comply with § 98.0706; civil remedies under § 98.0709.
rules.quoted_span: If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:
rules.conflict_note: The effective date of the Commission-notice provision depends on the portal launch date, which this document does not state.

rules.title: San Diego notice to tenant of residential tenant protections
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered property must give tenants a written notice in at least 12-point font describing state rent limits and local just cause protections, together with the Housing Commission's Tenant Protection Guide. For tenancies commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023, the notice must be in the lease or in a signed written notice at lease signing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of San Diego residential rental property subject to Division 7.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for separately alienable non-corporate-owned units requires a written exemption notice. Owner-occupancy exemptions apply.

rules.penalty: Civil remedies under § 98.0709; noncompliance voids termination notices (§ 98.0710).
rules.quoted_span: A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that states as follows:
rules.conflict_note: Existing tenancies required notice within 90 days of 2023-06-24.

rules.title: San Diego buyout agreement regulations
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout offer, a landlord must give each tenant a written disclosure of their rights. Buyout agreements must be in writing, include specified bold-print statements and be translated if negotiated in another language. A buyout agreement must exceed the relocation assistance owed, or it is void.
rules.key_value: Buyout must exceed required relocation assistance (2–3 months' rent)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of covered San Diego residential rental property making buyout offers to tenants.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as SDMC § 98.0703. Agreements settling a pending unlawful detainer action are not buyout agreements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for separately alienable non-corporate-owned units requires a written exemption notice.

rules.penalty: Noncompliant or undervalued buyout agreements are void; civil remedies under § 98.0709.
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.
